quotations.text: Magia secundum communiter loquentes est ars cognoscendi

claims.sentence_start: Copy-text Farmer 1998
claims.note: Latin matches Farmer 25117-25119.

claims.sentence_start: Akopyan and Busi print the same words
claims.note: Akopyan n. 44 has 'licita est, et non prohibita'; Busi n. 70 prints the whole thesis with v.

claims.sentence_start: 'pono' is the technical verb
claims.note: The locator shows only the word; 'technical verb for proposing a thesis' is an editorial gloss, not a source claim. Acceptable as a note.

claims.sentence_start: 'infrascriptas' means 'written below'
'scientia' is a body of demonstrative knowledge
claims.note: Declared editorial inference.

claims.sentence_start: Pico's own opinion: the second magical conclusion
claims.note: 'pono infrascriptas conclusiones secundum propriam opinionem'.

claims.sentence_start: al-Kindi, William of Auvergne (William of Paris) and Roger Bacon
claims.note: Farmer: in the Oration and Apology, 'among the moderns' Pico singles out three writers who had 'scented out' magia naturalis.

claims.sentence_start: William of Auvergne, De universo
claims.note: Copenhaver: 'In the Apology, Pico cited William ... to show that natural magic was not necromancy.' The title is not at the locator; Copenhaver's note 4 (copenhaver2019:24154) cites both De legibus (1674b) and De universo (1674c) without saying which one Pico cited. The work title is not established; remove it.

claims.sentence_start: Where 9>1 excludes demonic magic
Natural magic, in the sense used here
claims.note: William (as cited by Pico, in Copenhaver's translation): 'natural actions, the knowledge of which is one of the eleven parts of natural knowledge (scientia), where nothing is done with help from demons'.

claims.sentence_start: Pico's own formula in the Apology
claims.note: Farmer's translation of the Apology: 'the powers and activities of natural agents ... what they can and cannot do through their own power ... the one that I call natural magic'.

claims.sentence_start: The second clause turns the thesis into a preface
The series is therefore presented as the theory
claims.note: Declared editorial inference; 9796-9800 (Ebgi, entry CHARACTERES) says Pico raises a wall of reticence and refers answers to a secret philosophy.

claims.sentence_start: Farmer notes that medieval magical treatises
The authorities Pico names for natural magic among the moderns
claims.note: Dates (ninth and thirteenth centuries) as in Farmer.

claims.sentence_start: In the Oration the same three are said only to have picked up the scent
claims.note: Oration 58 (Copenhaver's translation): 'Among more recent authorities, I also find three who had picked up the scent of magic: Alkindi the Arab, Roger Bacon, and William of Paris.' 'only' is not in the source.

claims.sentence_start: Farmer uses this list to argue that Pico's natural magic was not Ficino's
claims.note: The chronology (De vita coelitus comparanda, Ficino's only magical treatise, written some two and a half years after the theses) is supported at 6603-6610, but it is Farmer's first point, not an argument drawn from the list of moderns; the list (6708-6714) is used against identifying Pico's natural magic with Hermetism.

claims.sentence_start: Pico's natural magic also concerned sublunary
claims.note: Farmer says 'suggesting'; the sentence states it flatly, acceptable since Farmer glosses 'natural agents' as 'sublunary forces'.

claims.sentence_start: In the Apology Pico declared that the specification and restriction
claims.note: Apologia text in Busi/Ebgi's anthology: 'Praedictam autem specificationem et restrictionem intentionis meae in conclusionibus magicis ad magiam naturalem, intendo esse applicandam cuilibet conclusioni particulari'.

claims.sentence_start: The bull of 4 August 1487 nonetheless complained
claims.note: Date checked: 'In a bull signed 4 August 1487' (1326); the quoted phrase is at 1350.

claims.sentence_start: In his attack on Pico's theses Pedro Garcia (1489)
claims.note: Farmer n.: 'Petrus Garcias (1489: H4v) adopted a succinct definition ... which probably could have been accepted by Pico himself'. Date checked.

claims.sentence_start: Farmer's reading of the whole section is framed against Frances Yates
Against that equation Farmer argues
Copenhaver reads the pairing of 9>1 and 9>2
claims.note: Copenhaver poses a question ('Did Pico want to advertise natural magic while keeping quiet about angel-magic?') and says the theses on magic (M) as a whole 'suggest so'; he does not attach it to the pairing of 9>1 and 9>2.

claims.sentence_start: Busi reads the licit magic of 9>2
claims.note: 'Nelle Conclusiones cattiva arte è però solo la magia nuova, quella dozzinale ...' followed by 9>2 in Italian. Busi's introduction (running head GIULIO BUSI).

claims.sentence_start: Akopyan treats the thesis as Pico's opposition
The thesis is the hinge of the series
claims.note: Declared editorial inference; the Apology sentence supports 'held Pico to that heading'.

claims.sentence_start: Which 'universal theoretical foundations'
claims.note: 'Ma la disputa non ebbe mai luogo.'

translation.note: Checked against farmer1998:25117-25119 and the sense of Farmer's English at 25157-25159. 'uniuersalibus theoricis fundamentis' rendered 'universal and theoretical foundations': the inserted 'and' is harmless. 'secundum propriam opinionem' kept. Similarity to Farmer 0.74 is below the gate threshold; the wording differs ('licit, not forbidden'; 'put forward'; 'set out below').
